TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a Transaction(s) between URI and the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management Relative to the Use of the W.
Alton Jones Campus Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for an Agreement on substantially the terms set forth in the enclosed Term Sheet, by which URI would allow the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management (RIDEM) to manage and use portions of the W.
Alton Jones Campus.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed Agreement with the RIDEM on substantially the terms outlined in the enclos ed Term Sheet.
This recommendation is based on a thorough review by and with appropriate stakeholders.
Points to Consider: URI has maintained the W.

Alton Jones Campus since 1962, using the campus for research, teaching, and community-oriented activities.
The campus was closed to the public in 2020, because of the COVID pandemic and amidst ongoing financial concerns.
On November 4, 2024, URI posted a Request for Information (RFI) seeking information on potential uses at the W.
Alton Jones campus that would support URI’s mission as a land grant institution, without impeding URI’s research and educational uses of the Property.
In response to this RFI, RIDEM expressed interest in using the Property for purposes that include administrative functions, educational programming, programs and camps (in collaboration with a third party approved by URI), agricultural activities, veterinary care and animal rehabilitation, wildlife and ecological research, and expanding public access to the property.
RIDEM would also invest in critical infrastructure on the campus, including existing buildings and utilities, and the protection of natural resources, including forest and dam management.

Partnering with RIDEM, the chief steward of the state’s natural resources, an agency with substantial experience in managing forested land and water resources throughout Rhode Island, and whose mission is to protect, restore, and promote those resources, allows URI to reopen the W.
Alton Jones Campus with increased protection of its natural resources and with expanded recreational and educational opportunities for the public.

Through this Agreement, URI would maintain use of the Campus for its current education and research needs and maintain the right to expand those uses as necessary. The fundamental structure and assumptions of this agreement are outlined in the attached Term Sheet. Supporting Information: See attached Term Sheet. Proposed Motion of the Board: To recommend approval of an Agreement regarding the use of portions of the W. Alton Jones Campus at 401 Victory Hwy, West Greenwich, RI by the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management as presented on substantially the terms in the enclosed Term Sheet, and that any authorized signatory (as defined in the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents) be authorized to negotiate the terms of any documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms in the enclosure, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary or appropriate by the authorized signatory.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B. Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: September 11, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: FY2026 Total Budget Request Purpose of Submittal: This is a request for the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the FY2026 Total Budget Request for submission to the State Office of Management and Budget. Points to Consider: The FY2026 total budget request for URI is $1.13B. Within this, the FY2026 State General Appropriations request is $146.2M and includes the following components: FY25 Enacted Operating Budget $110.8M Anticipated Operating Shortfall $5.7M Current Service Level $21.6M Strategic Initiatives $13.6M Total $151.7 Anticipated tuition & fee/misc revenue ($5.5M) Total FY26 Budget Request $146.2M The FY2026 General Appropriations includes a $13.6M request for Strategic Initiatives, which includes the following critical operating budget components, in alignment with the Focus URI Strategic Plan: SP1: Broaden Our Impact (Life Sciences Faculty and remaining land-grant state support) $5.3M SP2: Enhance Student Achievement (Academic Advisors) $2.0M SP3: Foster an Inclusive Culture (Support for TD Program, National Guard & Tribal scholarship support) $2.3M SP4: Power the University of the Future (IT Modernization) $4.0M Total $13.6M

As a reminder, last year the Board of Trustees shifted final approval of tuition and fees to the February meeting to make better informed decisions, therefore this budget request assumes a baseline tuition increase of 3.0% and fee increase of 0.7% which will be revisited in February. Finally, the FY2026 URI total budget request includes a significant increase in State RICAP support ($45.2M, 88% over FY2025), as reflected in the Capital Improvement Plan approved by the Board in June 2024. Supporting Information: Please refer to the attached presentation. Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island FY2026 Total Budget Request as set forth in enclosure and as recommended and presented.

TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 26, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of the FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: To purpose of this action is to seek Board of Trustees approval for the submission of the University of Rhode Island FY2027―FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) to the State of Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: Every year it is the responsibility of the University to submit a CIP to the State of Rhode Island.
The CIP identifies and lists in order of priority capital projects (both proposed or in progress) of $1 million or more funded with unrestricted funds.
This submission is a critical and required step to secure funding to support the physical assets at the University advancing both educational and research programs.

The enclosed presentation provides updat es to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 projects, the Fine Arts Center, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, and New Undergraduate Housing.
It also provides information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects, which have been on hold for the last several years to prioritize housing.
The presentation also highlights several additions made to the CIP last year, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions incl ude improving campus accessibility, access control, building envelope integrity, and refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems and the university’s water tower.

Two new projects are proposed to be added to the CIP this year, replacement of the Allen Harbor Bulkhead and Dock, which is necessary to protect the site and maintain access to our small boats that provide both educational and research support, and a project currently underway to renovate Washburn Hall and the Carlotti Building to provide space needed to empty Tucker House and Adams House in anticipation of future mixed-use development on Upper College Road.
The CIP also recommends a 2026 General Obligation (GO) Bond project for an Integrated Health Building.
The Integrated Health Buildin g would provide expanded programming to support interprofessional education and clinical training in the health disciplines.
URI is currently contemplating the construction of a new Student Success building on the current site of the Carlotti Building on the quad for the 2028 GO Bond.

Slides 8, 9, and 11 of the enclosed presentation highlight in blue changes from the Draft CIP reviewed by the committee in April, as follows: • We are repeating our full ask for Campus Accessibility and Building Envelope impr ovements, both of which will likely be funded in part by the legislature this year. • The former Blue Technology Innovation Center is now named the Ocean Technology Innovation Center, which was recently awarded funding by the Department of Commerce. • The project costs for Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 2 have been increased slightly to include additional donations to support equipment, and the project cost for repairing the bulkhead at Allen Harbor has been increased after an initial design effort. Recommendation: I recommend that the Board of Trustees approve the enclosed University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031. Supporting Information: Please see University of Rhode Island FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan Enclosure Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees approve the University of Rhode Island Capital Improvement Plan for FY2027-FY2031 as presented.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY27-FY31 Presentation to Board of Trustees – Finance and Facilities June 26, 2025

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? • 5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million • It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically in July. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? • There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island - Facilities Committee (internal) (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - President’s Executive Council (March & May) • University of Rhode Island - Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Recommended Capital Budget by the Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January – June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? • In order to receive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development • Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.
